interface.signature: def shoot(rounds: List[Tuple[Dict[str, str], bool]]) -> str:

preconditions.expression: isinstance(rounds, list) and all(isinstance(round, tuple) and len(round) == 2 and isinstance(round[0], dict) and isinstance(round[1], bool) for round in rounds)
preconditions.description: The input `rounds` must be a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a dictionary and a boolean.

preconditions.expression: all('P1' in round[0] and 'P2' in round[0] and all(hit in 'XO' for hit in round[0].values()) for round in rounds)
preconditions.description: Each dictionary in the input must contain 'P1' and 'P2' keys, with values being 'X' or 'O'.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(round[1], bool) for round in rounds)
preconditions.description: Each boolean in the input must be a boolean value.

postconditions.description: The function must return a string indicating the winner or if it's a draw.

postconditions.expression: result == 'Pete Wins!' if sum(2 if round[1] else 1 for round in rounds if 'X' in round[0]['P1']) > sum(2 if round[1] else 1 for round in rounds if 'X' in round[0]['P2']) else 'Phil Wins!' if sum(2 if round[1] else 1 for round in rounds if 'X' in round[0]['P1']) < sum(2 if round[1] else 1 for round in rounds if 'X' in round[0]['P2']) else 'Draw!'
postconditions.description: The function must return the correct winner based on the total score of hits.
